intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to use the て-form to say several actions in order in one sentence, like "I get up, brush my teeth, and eat". You will also learn to join adjectives with くて / で, to say "after doing" (てから / あとで), to ask "how?" (どうやって), and to describe someone's appearance, as in "he has big eyes". By the end you will be able to explain everyday procedures in Japanese, such as changing trains or depositing money at an ATM.

g16-1.explanation_en: To say several actions in one sentence in the order they happen, put the earlier verbs in the て-form and end only the last verb with ます / ました / てください. In Tamil, when you say "எழுந்து, பல் துலக்கி, சாப்பிடுகிறேன்" (I get up, brush my teeth, and eat), the verbal participles "எழுந்து" and "துலக்கி" carry no tense; only the last verb "சாப்பிடுகிறேன்" shows the tense. The Japanese て-form works the same way: whether it is present or past shows only on the last verb. Say the actions in the order they happened. Usually you don't join more than two or three て-forms in one sentence.
g16-1.tamil_parallel_en: Japanese て works like the Tamil verbal participle ending -து / -இ: எழுந்து, பல் துலக்கி, சாப்பிடுகிறேன் ("having got up, having brushed my teeth, I eat") = 起きて、歯を磨いて、食べます. Only the final verb carries tense, in both languages.
g16-1.formation_en: V1 て-form + 、+ V2 て-form + 、+ V3 ます / ました / てください (tense only on the last verb)
g16-1.pitfalls_en: The て-form has no tense, so don't put every verb in the past as in "ました、ました"; marking the last verb is enough. Don't use て to say that one action is the reason for another; for that you have から (Lesson 9).

g16-2.explanation_en: To give two qualities of one thing in a single sentence, put the first adjective in its joining form. For an い-adjective, drop the final い and add くて (大きい → 大きくて); only いい becomes よくて. For a な-adjective or a noun, add で (静か → 静かで、学生 → 学生で). This is just like adding "-ஆகவும்" in Tamil: "இந்த அறை வெளிச்சமாகவும் சுத்தமாகவும் இருக்கிறது" (this room is bright and clean). Both qualities must point the same way (both good or both bad). If they contrast, like "small but comfortable", don't use くて; use が (but).
g16-2.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "-ஆகவும் ... -ஆகவும்": இந்த அறை வெளிச்சமாகவும் சுத்தமாகவும் இருக்கிறது ("this room is bright and clean") = この部屋は明るくて、きれいです.
g16-2.formation_en: い-adj: 〜い → 〜くて (大きい → 大きくて、いい → よくて) / な-adj: 〜 + で (静か → 静かで) / N: N + で (学生 → 学生で、日本人 → 日本人で)
g16-2.pitfalls_en: Don't add で to an い-adjective: ×明るいで → ○明るくて. For いい it is not ×いくて but ○よくて. For contrasting ideas, like "that shop is cheap, but the food isn't tasty", don't use くて; use が.

g16-3.explanation_en: Adding から after the て-form of V1 means "only after V1 is finished, V2". Plain て joining just gives the order; てから stresses that the first action must be finished first, and only then the next one happens. It matches Tamil "சாப்பிட்டு விட்டுப் போகிறேன்" (I'll eat and then go) or "வீட்டுப்பாடம் செய்து முடித்த பிறகு விளையாடுவேன்" (I'll play after finishing my homework). Here too, tense shows only on the last verb. It is normal to use てから only once in a sentence.
g16-3.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "செய்து முடித்த பிறகு" (after finishing doing): வீட்டுப்பாடம் செய்து முடித்த பிறகு விளையாடுவேன் ("I'll play after I finish my homework") = 宿題をしてから、遊びます.
g16-3.formation_en: V1 て-form + から、+ V2 (ます / ました / てください)
g16-3.pitfalls_en: Don't mix up 食べますから (ます + から = "because", a reason) and 食べてから (て + から = "after"). For the meaning "after", the verb before から is always in the て-form.

g16-4.explanation_en: To say "after ...", use あとで. With a noun, add の: ご飯のあとで (after the meal), 仕事のあとで (after work). With a verb you need the た-form (た形); you will study it fully in Lesson 19. For now, a simple rule: change て → た and で → だ in the て-form and you get the た-form (見て → 見た、読んで → 読んだ、して → した). Just as Tamil "பார்த்த பிறகு" (after seeing) has the past participle "பார்த்த" + "பிறகு", Japanese has 見た + あとで. あとで is looser than てから; it can also mean "sometime after that".
g16-4.tamil_parallel_en: Tamil uses a past participle + பிறகு, and Japanese uses the た-form + あとで: சாப்பாட்டுக்குப் பிறகு ("after the meal") = ご飯のあとで ; படம் பார்த்த பிறகு ("after watching the film") = 映画を見たあとで.
g16-4.formation_en: N + の + あとで、〜 / V た-form (て→た: 見て→見た、飲んで→飲んだ、行って→行った、して→した、来て→来た) + あとで、〜
g16-4.pitfalls_en: Don't forget の after a noun: ×ご飯あとで → ○ご飯のあとで. Don't use the ます-form with the verb: ×見ますあとで → ○見たあとで.

g16-5.explanation_en: To talk about one part or feature of a person (or a place), make the whole the topic with は, mark the part with が, and then add the adjective. 田中さんは目が大きいです = speaking of Tanaka-san, her eyes are big. It is just like Tamil "அவருக்குக் கண் பெரிது" (he has big eyes) or "அண்ணனுக்கு உயரம் அதிகம்" (my elder brother is tall), where the person takes "-க்கு" and the part is the subject. You can also say 田中さんの目は大きいです, but then you are talking about the eyes; with the は〜が pattern you are talking about the person. It works not only for people but also for places, as in チェンナイは人が多いです (Chennai has a lot of people).
g16-5.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "person-க்கு + part + adjective": அண்ணனுக்கு உயரம் அதிகம் ("my elder brother is tall", literally "to elder brother, height is a lot") = 兄は背が高いです.
g16-5.formation_en: N1 (person / place: the whole) + は + N2 (part / feature) + が + adj です
g16-5.pitfalls_en: For height use 背が高い / 背が低い, not ×背が長い or ×背が短い. The part takes が; don't say ×目を大きい, and don't put two は in one sentence like ×目は大きい.

g16-6.explanation_en: どうやって is a question word that asks for the way or method: "how, by what means". Use it for questions like "How do I get to the station?" or "How do I use this machine?". The answer usually has "N で" (route / tool) or a て-form sequence (V1て、V2ます). Keep these three apart: どう (how is it? Lesson 8) asks about a state; どうして (why? Lesson 9) asks for a reason; どうやって asks for a method. It comes before the verb, usually after the place or object.
g16-6.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "எப்படி" asking for the way to do something: ஸ்டேஷனுக்கு எப்படிப் போவது? ("How do I get to the station?") = 駅までどうやって行きますか.
g16-6.formation_en: (N まで / N を) + どうやって + V ますか → Answer: N で V ます / V1 て、V2 ます
g16-6.pitfalls_en: どうやって (how to do it) vs どうして (why): because they sound alike, Tamil learners often mix them up. Asking about a state with どうですか (how is it?) is different again.

g16-7.explanation_en: You can end a sentence with 。 and start the next one with そして or それから to link them. そして = "and / and then"; it adds actions or qualities (この町は静かです。そして、きれいです。). それから = "after that"; it gives the order in which actions happen, and it is also used to add "and one more thing" to a list. It is just like starting a new sentence in Tamil with "அப்புறம்", "பிறகு" or "அதன் பிறகு". When a 〜て、〜て chain gets long, the natural style is to end the sentence and continue with そして / それから.
g16-7.tamil_parallel_en: Like starting a new Tamil sentence with "அதன் பிறகு" (after that): வங்கிக்குப் போகிறேன். அதன் பிறகு தபால் நிலையத்துக்குப் போகிறேன் ("I'll go to the bank. After that I'll go to the post office.") = 銀行へ行きます。それから、郵便局へ行きます.
g16-7.formation_en: Sentence 1。+ そして / それから、+ Sentence 2。
g16-7.pitfalls_en: そして / それから come at the start of a sentence; don't stick them into the middle as in いきますそして. どうして (why) is a different word.

items.L16-q01: 押す = おす (அழுத்த, to press); its て-form is おして. おきて is 起きて (எழுந்து, getting up), a different verb.
items.L16-q02: 強い = つよい (வலிமையான, strong). よわい is 弱い (பலவீனமான, weak), the opposite word; there is no word つおい.
items.L16-q03: 足 = あし (கால், leg / foot). Don't voice し and read it as あじ; はし is 箸 (சாப்ஸ்டிக், chopsticks).
items.L16-q04: め = 目 (கண், eye). 日 (ひ) and 月 (つき) look similar but are different words; 耳 = みみ (காது, ear).
items.L16-q05: みがく = 磨く (துலக்க, to brush / polish). 摩・麻・魔 are look-alike kanji that all contain the 麻 part; for "brush" the right one is 磨, with 石 (stone) underneath.
items.L16-q06: To say a person is short, use 背が低い. 短い is for length (a pencil, a river); don't use it for height.
items.L16-q07: I get off the train (降りて, இறங்கி) and get on the bus. The opposite of 乗ります is 降ります; 入れる means "to put in".
items.L16-q08: Because there is no window, the room is dark (暗い, இருட்டு). 明るい (வெளிச்சமான, bright) is the opposite word and does not fit the reason.
items.L16-q09: 歯を磨きます = I brush my teeth (பல் துலக்குகிறேன்). The verb that goes with 歯 is 磨く; 押す (அழுத்த, to press) does not fit.
items.L16-q10: I put sugar in my coffee = 入れます (போடுகிறேன்). Remember the pattern "N に N を 入れる"; 引く = to pull (இழுக்க).
items.L16-q11: The linking word that joins two actions in order is それから (அதன் பிறகு, after that). どうして (why) and どうやって (how) are question words.
items.L16-q12: 背が高くない (not tall) = 背が低い (குட்டை, short). 足が長い (long legs) says nothing about height.
items.L16-q13: 明るくない (not bright) = 暗い (இருட்டு, dark). 汚い (அழுக்கு, dirty) is not about light.
items.L16-q14: V てから = after V is finished; 宿題のあとで has the same meaning. 遊んでから、宿題をします reverses the order; しませんから gives a reason, "because I don't do it".
items.L16-q15: A verb in the middle of the sentence must be in the て-form: 磨く → 磨いて (き → いて). 磨きて is a wrong form; the ます-form comes only at the end.
items.L16-q16: 静か is a な-adjective, so you join it with で. くて is only for い-adjectives (大きくて).
items.L16-q17: い-adjective 安い → drop い and add くて: 安くて. Putting で after an い-adjective, as in 安いで, is a common mistake for Tamil learners.
items.L16-q18: In the "N1 は N2 が adj" pattern, が marks the part (背). Using を, as in 背を高い, is wrong: 高い is an adjective, not a verb.
items.L16-q19: For the meaning "after doing ...", use the て-form + から: 入れてから. 入れますから would mean "because I put it in" (a reason).
items.L16-q20: Before あとで the verb comes in the た-form: 見た あとで. Don't use the て-form as in 見て あとで; a ます-form like 見ました does not appear in the middle of a sentence.
items.L16-q21: The answer バスで (by bus) gives a way of going, so the question is どうやって (எப்படி, how). どうして means "why", and its answer would be 〜から.
items.L16-q22: 田中さんは 目が 大きくて、きれいです。 This is the "N1 は N2 が adj" pattern; the first adjective 大きい takes its joining form 大きくて, and the last adjective ends with です.
items.L16-q23: 朝 起きて、シャワーの あとで 朝ご飯を 食べます。 First the て-form (起きて), then "N の あとで", and at the end を + a ます verb.
items.L16-q24: 駅で 電車に 乗って、会社へ 行きます。 The verb 乗る takes に (電車に乗る); the first action is in the て-form and the last action uses ます.
items.L16-q25: [1] and [2] are actions in the middle of the sentence, so they take the て-form (磨いて、乗って); since 乗る comes with に, 降りて does not fit. [3] starts a new sentence, and the word that links it with "after that" is それから.
